units.translation: 177. Opposite the Thynian land: There are two Thynias, one in Europe and one in Asia; the one in Europe lies near Salmydessus in Thrace, while the other extends to the Bosporus and the mouth of the Pontus. [There is also a third Thynia, an island in the Pontus.] It is ambiguous to which Thynia he refers, since both are on the opposite side. It is better, then, to say the Thynia in Europe; for on the following day, he says, they moored the stern cables in Thynia 〈...〉, as is clear, from Asia to Europe. For Phineus, as most say, is said to have dwelt at Salmydessus, which is in Thrace on the left side as one sails into the Pontus. There is also a third Thynia, an island in the Pontus, on which there is a sanctuary of Apollo.

178-82a. Son of Agenor, hold: For he is a child of Agenor, as Hellanicus says; but as Hesiod says, of Phoenix son of Agenor and Cassiepeia. Asclepiades, Antimachus, and Pherecydes say likewise. From Cassiepeia daughter of Arabus and Phoenix are born Cilix, Phineus, Doryclus, and Atymnus by surname; Atymnus is born from Zeus.

b. 〈Here:〉 not in the Thynia near 〈Asia〉, but in the one opposite [Thrace], which is in Europe, as has been shown. Some record that he ruled in Paphlagonia, which is in Asia. He called Phineus son of Agenor, inasmuch as he is a child of Agenor, as Hellanicus says; but Hesiod says he is son of Phoenix son of Agenor. They say Phineus was blinded by Helios because he chose to live a long life rather than to see. Some say it is incredible that he lived so many generations, and that there were more of them, and that the Phineus who was the seventh descendant of Phoenix was a different one, whom the heroes met.

And that he was blinded because he plotted against Perseus. Sophocles says that he blinded the sons of Cleopatra, Parthenius and Carambis, persuaded by the slanders of Idaea their stepmother. But Apollonius says he was blinded and suffered harm from the Harpies because he prophesied openly and explicitly to all; for he says, 'not even as much as he revered even Zeus himself.'
